True
trū
adj. (conformable to fact; also genuine, real, as opposed to the shadow; rendering Hebrew emet, Greek alethes, alethinos)
From Anglo-Saxon treowe, faithful, trusty — the same root as trust and troth. The English word begins with fidelity, not with accuracy, and so does the Hebrew.

Biblical Definition

True in Scripture carries two senses that must be kept together. The first is factual: Deuteronomy requires that a capital charge be examined until “it be true, and the thing certain” (Deu 17:4). Joseph's brothers plead it of themselves — “we are true men, thy servants are no spies” (Gen 42:11) — where true means honest, not merely accurate. Boaz uses it of a legal fact he cannot evade: “it is true that I am thy near kinsman: howbeit there is a kinsman nearer than I” (Rut 3:12). The second sense is the Greek alethinos: not the opposite of false but the opposite of the shadow, the real as against the copy. So the Lord Jesus says, “I am the true vine” (John 15:1) — Israel was a vine, and He is the reality it pictured. Both senses meet in Philippians 4:8, where Paul makes truth the first filter of Christian thought: “whatsoever things are true… think on these things”.

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) defines true as conformable to fact, not false, and also as genuine, pure, real, not counterfeit — and as faithful, steady in adhering to friends, to promises, or to a prince.

expand to see more

TRUE, a. Conformable to fact; being in accordance with the actual state of things; as a true relation.

2. Genuine; pure; real; not counterfeit, adulterated or false; as true balsam.

3. Faithful; steady in adhering to friends, to promises, to a prince, or to the state; loyal.

4. Honest; not fraudulent. We are true men; thy servants are no spies. Gen. xlii.

Key Scripture

John 15:1 — "I am the true vine, and my Father is the husbandman."

Php 4:8 — "Finally, brethren, whatsoever things are true, whatsoever things are honest, whatsoever things are just, whatsoever things are pure, whatsoever things are lovely, whatsoever things are of good report; if there be any virtue, and if there be any praise, think on these things."

Deu 17:4 — "And it be told thee, and thou hast heard of it, and enquired diligently, and, behold, it be true, and the thing certain, that such abomination is wrought in Israel:"

Rut 3:12 — "And now it is true that I am thy near kinsman: howbeit there is a kinsman nearer than I."

Modern Corruption

Truth relocated from correspondence with reality to sincerity or perspective — my truth — which makes the word unusable for the one thing Scripture uses it for.

expand to see more

The dominant move of the age is to make truth a possession rather than a property: a thing is true for someone, and the honest expression of a conviction becomes indistinguishable from its accuracy. Deuteronomy 17:4 forecloses that immediately — a charge must be enquired into diligently until it is true, and the thing certain, because a man's life turns on the difference between a sincere accusation and an accurate one. Wherever the distinction collapses, the vulnerable are the first to suffer.

The deeper loss is the second sense. Alethinos means real as against the shadow, and it is the word by which the New Testament claims that the Old Testament's furniture was always a picture: the true vine, the true light, the true tabernacle, the true bread from heaven. That vocabulary is how Scripture teaches the believer to read the Old Testament without either discarding it or freezing in it. And Philippians 4:8 makes the whole matter practical: what is true is the first thing a Christian mind is commanded to dwell upon.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew emet (H571), truth, firmness, faithfulness — from aman, to support, the root of amen; Greek alethes (G227), not concealed, true; alethinos (G228), real, genuine, as opposed to the shadow.

expand to see more

Hebrew emet (H571) — truth, firmness; built on aman, to be firm, from which amen comes — truth as what holds weight.

Greek alethes (G227) — true, unconcealed; the opposite of falsehood, as in Php 4:8.

Greek alethinos (G228) — genuine, real, the substance rather than the shadow; the true vine (John 15:1), the true light, the true tabernacle (Heb 8:2).

Usage

"“I am the true vine” — not merely truthful; the reality the shadow pictured."

"“Whatsoever things are true… think on these things” — the first filter of Christian thought."

"“It be true, and the thing certain” — sincerity is not the same as accuracy."
